status_summary: National Security Presidential Memorandum 1 (2025-01-20) puts the NSC and the Homeland Security Council on one staff under one Executive Secretary; it does not mention detailees or a staff size. On 2025-01-22 the Associated Press reported that about 160 NSC detailees, mostly career experts from other agencies, had been sent home pending a staffing review, and on 2025-05-23 it reported an overhaul of a staff of roughly 395 in which about 90 to 95 detailed experts were removed and could return to their home agencies, with the staff expected to be significantly reduced; a New York Times report relayed the same weekend said the staff would be cut by at least half. No post-cut headcount or written detailee limit was found. On 2026-09-22 Fox News and the Washington Examiner reported that the Secretary of State, acting national security adviser since May 2025, had been commissioned as national security adviser; neither report gives staffing figures.

timeline.event: National Security Presidential Memorandum 1 reorganizes the NSC system, with a single NSC staff in the Executive Office of the President serving both the NSC and the Homeland Security Council under one Executive Secretary. The text read sets no staff size and does not address detailees.

The Associated Press reports that about 160 NSC detailees, mostly career subject-matter experts on loan from agencies such as State, the FBI and the CIA, were sent home pending a review of NSC staffing meant to align it with the President's agenda; some counterterrorism detailees were returned to their home agencies early.

The Associated Press reports an NSC overhaul: a staff of roughly 395 (about 180 support staff), with about 90 to 95 detailed policy or subject-matter experts removed and free to return to home agencies, and the staff count expected to be significantly reduced.

A New York Times report, carried by a regional paper on 2025-05-24 without a precise date, says the NSC staff will be cut by at least half, with some agency detailees returning to their home offices and others placed on administrative leave. It gives no headcount.
timeline.source: New York Times via Hawaii Tribune-Herald

timeline.event: Fox News and the Washington Examiner report that the President signed a commission making the Secretary of State, acting national security adviser since 2025-05-01, national security adviser; neither report describes NSC staff size or detailees.

title: Limit the number of NSC staff detailees to give the President more direct control
uncertainties: NSPM-1 was read on whitehouse.gov and contains no detailee provision or staff size. The detailee and staff reductions rest on press reports citing unnamed officials (AP syndicated copies of 2025-01-22 and 2025-05-23, and a New York Times report carried by a regional paper). No outlet gave a post-cut headcount, so whether the staff now sits in the chapter's 100 to 150 range, and whether detailees were later replaced, is not shown. A July-August 2026 Foreign Service Journal commentary describes a smaller NSC but gives no figures. The stage is a judgment: the reported removals are operative in substance, but without a current detailee count or written limit the record stays in_progress rather than implemented. Overlaps with c02-03, which covers returning nonessential detailees on the first day.
